title: George Clooney, Ellen Burstyn, Luca Guadagnino and More Set for Venice Masterclasses
description:
Venice Film Festival has revealed the lineup for this year’s masterclasses, featuring George Clooney, Ellen Burstyn, Luca Guadagnino and more. 

	Th
body:
Venice Film Festival has revealed the lineup for this year’s masterclasses, featuring George Clooney, Ellen Burstyn, Luca Guadagnino and more. 

	The masterclasses will once again take place at the Lido’s Match Point Arena, which can seat 250 accredited guests, and will also be livestreamed on the festival’s website. In addition to Clooney and Burstyn, who are both receiving Venice’s Golden Lion for Lifetime Achievement at this year’s edition, French filmmaker Luc Besson is also set to give a masterclass.All talks will begin at 4 p.m., with Clooney’s scheduled for Sept. 3, Besson’s Sept. 6 and Burstyn’s Sept. 8. 
	

	Meanwhile, Guadagnino and “Hamnet” director Chloé Zhao will participate in masterclasses presented b Cartier and themed around “The Art and Craft of Cinema.” Zhao will be in conversation with Polish cinematographer Lukasz Zal, her collaborator on “Hamnet,” with the event taking place Sept. 4 at 3:30 p.m. Guadagnino, who will be honored with Cartier’s Glory to the Filmmaker Award during this year’s fest, will deliver his class on Sept. 7 at 3:30 p.m.


	The 83rd Venice Film Festival kicks off on Sept. 2 with the premiere of “Ink,” Danny Boyle’s Rupert Murdoch drama starring Jack O’Connell, Guy Pearce and Claire Foy, which is also in the running for the prestigious Golden Lion for best film. Other titles in competition include Lance Oppenheim’s “Primetime,” starring Robert Pattinson; Casey Affleck’s “Company”; Werner Herzog’s “Bucking Fastard,” with Kate and Rooney Mara; Hirokazu Kore-eda’s “Look Back”; Martin McDonagh’s “Wild Horse Nine”; Florian Zeller’s “Bunker” led by Penélope Cruz and Javier Bardem and more.

schema.headline: George Clooney, Ellen Burstyn, Luca Guadagnino and More Set for Venice Masterclasses

title: Hannah Einbinder Defends Mark Ruffalo After Paramount Calls His Merger Attack ‘Antisemitic’: ‘Those of Us With a Platform Need to Use Our Voices’
description: “Hacks” star Hannah Einbinder has come to the defense of Mark Ruffalo after Paramount accused him of invoking “antisemitic tropes” when criticizing
body:
“Hacks” star Hannah Einbinder has come to the defense of Mark Ruffalo after Paramount accused him of invoking “antisemitic tropes” when criticizing the Paramount-Warner Bros. merger.

	It all kicked off on Friday, when Ruffalo shared a clip on Instagram of Paramount board member Safra Catz outlining “really profoundly scary technologies” that Oracle — the tech giant co-founded by Larry Ellison, father of Paramount Skydance CEO David Ellison, who is involved in the merger’s financing — used to help the Israeli military after the Oct. 7 terror attack. Ruffalo likened Larry Ellison to a “classic oligarch” and warned of the consequences if Paramount and Warner Bros. are allowed to merge, alleging that the Ellisons “are crushing workers and consolidating the wealth of the world for their own power and concentrated dominance.” Of Catz, he said: “Look how she revels in what we now have come to see as a genocide, which was built on an apartheid system of oppression powered by Oracle.”
	

	A Paramount spokesperson then said in a statement that they are “troubled when antisemitic tropes are invoked in purported service of a business dispute. Words like ‘genocide’ and ‘apartheid,’ applied to a corporate transaction, aren’t just wrong — they’re a bridge too far, and they cheapen the very real suffering those words are meant to describe. This doesn’t deserve a response in kind — and to be clear, we don’t tolerate prejudice of any kind, against anyone.”


	On her Instagram Story on Monday night, Einbinder — who is Jewish and has been an outspoken advocate for Palestinians — became the first major celebrity to publicly support Ruffalo. “I’m so grateful that Mark Ruffalo drew a connection between the Ellisons providing military technology to Israel during a genocide and their unprecedented media takeover — and pointed out that this is a dangerous consolidation of power that could ultimately be used against us,” she wrote. 
	

	“The idea that he only said these things because the Ellisons are Jewish is LUDICROUS,” Einbinder continued. “Is it also antisemitic to point out that Safra Catz, the Oracle executive vice chair who boasted about the ‘profoundly scary technology’ provided to the IDF, also sits on Paramount’s board? Or that Larry Ellison has been buying favor with Trump by donating tens of millions to his political effort for years? Or that he once offered Netanyahu a lucrative Oracle post?”

	Einbinder added that “if you want to make it about the Ellisons being Jewish, then you are the one being antisemitic.” She concluded her statement by saying, “All of us artists could stand to be more like Mark, willing to speak out for oppressed people everywhere, even when powerful people try to bully us into silence. Visibility is a responsibility. Those of us with a platform need to use our voices before speaking out is outlawed altogether.”

	Following his initial post, Ruffalo was also called out by Jewish advocacy groups the Simon Wiesenthal Center and Creative Communities for Peace. 

	“Words matter, and so does the willingness to draw a line when legitimate debate gives way to antisemitic tropes,” said Jim Berk, CEO of the Simon Wiesenthal Center. “We commend Paramount for speaking clearly and refusing to allow prejudice to masquerade as political or corporate criticism. At a time when antisemitism is too often minimized, rationalized, or repackaged in more socially acceptable language, this kind of moral clarity matters.”

	In response to Paramount, Ruffalo wrote on X on Saturday: “The accusation that I am antisemitic is appalling and fundamentally dishonest. Criticizing the actions of the Israeli prime minister, a military technology contract, or the executives who supply it is not the same as criticizing Jewish people. This critical and necessary dialogue is then dishonestly framed as being anti-Israel. To be clear, my views come from my own political convictions and should never be interpreted as hostility toward Jewish people, for whom I have deep love and respect. Everything I know about acting, activism, and humanism has been profoundly shaped by the Jewish friends, colleagues, and loved ones who have been integral and family throughout every point of my life.”

schema.headline: Hannah Einbinder Defends Mark Ruffalo After Paramount Calls His Merger Attack ‘Antisemitic’: ‘Those of Us With a Platform Need to Use Our Voices’

title: George Clooney, Maggie Gyllenhaal, Alexandre Desplat and More Set for Finch & Partners and CAA’s ‘Future of Creativity’ Forum in Venice
description: George Clooney, Maggie Gyllenhaal, Alexandre Desplat and more are set to take part in an inaugural forum themed around creativity in Venice next mon
body:
George Clooney, Maggie Gyllenhaal, Alexandre Desplat and more are set to take part in an inaugural forum themed around creativity in Venice next month, held alongside the film festival. 

	Presented by Finch & Partners and CAA, the invitation-only forum is titled “The Future of… Creativity” and, according to a press release, aims to gather “leading voices from literature, cinema, the visual arts and technology to explore one of the defining questions of our time: what is the future of creativity in the age of transformational change?” 
	

	Taking place on Sept. 4 at the historic Scuola Vecchia della Misericordia, the forum will be hosted by Venice Film Festival artistic director Alberto Barbera and will feature panel discussions with Clooney, who is set to receive the fest’s Golden Lion for lifetime achievement; Gyllenhaal, who is also serving as Venice jury president; Oscar-winning composer and frequent Wes Anderson collaborator Desplat; legendary Italian writer-director Giuseppe Tornatore; Cardinal Jose Tolentino de Mendonca, who is the culture and education prefect at the Vatican; sculptor and painter Kennedy Yanko; visual artist Marc Quinn; president of Signal Meredith Whittaker; and Emmy-winning film and TV director Shannon Murphy (“Killing Eve”).


	The forum builds on the inaugural “Future of… Film” event held during the Cannes Film Festival in May, which featured Darren Aronofsky, James Gray, Nadine Labaki, Whit Stillman and J.A. Bayona as well as executives from Mubi, A24, Sony Pictures Classics, Neon, Focus Features and Sony Pictures. The Venice edition is set to “broaden the conversation beyond film to examine how AI and other technological changes are transforming creativity across disciplines and what that means for the future of culture itself,” according to the release. 
	

	“Storytelling has accompanied every stage of human civilization, and the tools for telling stories have never stopped changing,” Barbera said in a statement. “Artificial intelligence may prove the greatest change yet, with an impact on human activity perhaps greater even than that of the 19th-century Industrial Revolution. There is much discussion, quite rightly, about its worrying aspects: the repercussions for employment, for artists’ copyright and image rights and the ethical dimension of the phenomenon. I believe it is important, however, to begin with a different question: what does this mean for creativity itself, and what new tools, if any, might it offer to support the work of artists, and of filmmakers in particular. To this end, we have asked a select group of qualified artists to discuss the topic freely, expressing their views, in the hope that this might help to open a new chapter in the debate on the future of creativity and storytelling.”

	Added Claire Ingle-Finch, managing partner at Finch & Partners: “Human beings have always told stories. It is how we make sense of ourselves, and how one generation speaks to the next. The stories are handed down through centuries and millennia; only the form changes. In 2026, the form is changing again, and artificial intelligence is that change. This year’s ‘The Future Of… Creativity’ brings together people who have given their lives to storytelling, to talk plainly about what this moment means for the craft and for the people who love it. It is a conversation, honestly had, among people who know the work from the inside. Venice, which has traded in stories for a thousand years, seemed the right place for it.”

	Co-head of CAA Media Finance Roeg Sutherland said that the forums “convene those who shape culture and are dedicated to sustaining and protecting art — in all its forms, while embracing new forms of expression and innovation that celebrates the human experience.” 

	He continued, “As we saw at our event in Cannes, world-class business leaders, creators and visionaries from across industries share a collective interest in harnessing technology to deepen creativity, and this gathering in Venice expands on those meaningful and productive conversations.”

schema.headline: George Clooney, Maggie Gyllenhaal, Alexandre Desplat and More Set for Finch & Partners and CAA’s ‘Future of Creativity’ Forum in Venice

title: Anthony Boyle to Lead Sky Drama ‘Charmer’ From Working Title, Story Films
description: Anthony Boyle, the “House of Guinness” star soon to be seen playing Sam Bankman-Fried in Netflix’s “The Altruists,” is set to lead upcoming Sky Orig
body:
Anthony Boyle, the “House of Guinness” star soon to be seen playing Sam Bankman-Fried in Netflix’s “The Altruists,” is set to lead upcoming Sky Original drama “Charmer.”

	The eight-part series, now in production, comes from Working Title Television and Story Films, with Siena Kelly (“Black Mirror,” “Adult Material”), Connor Swindells (“The Entertainment System Is Down,” “SAS Rogue Heroes”) and Sophie Wilde (“Digger,” “Talk to Me”) also among the key cast.
	

	“Charmer” follows an ambitious group of 30-something Londoners whose lives are turned upside down by Ryan (Boyle), a seducer-for-hire employed to test the fidelity of his wealthy clients’ partners. “As a wedding day draws closer, an assignment becomes personal, threatening the professional distance that has always underpinned Ryan’s work,” reads the synopsis. “As deception gives way to desire, Ryan risks breaking the one rule that has always defined him: never fall in love.”


	Sam Delich, Vivian Oparah, Neil Maskell, Karan Gill, Sophie Simnett and Polly Walker round out the cast.

	Created and written by Thomas Aspell, “Charmer” is directed by Elliot Hegarty, whose credits also include “Rivals,” “Ted Lasso” and “Bad Education.” Additional episodes are written by Melissa Bubnic, Constance Cheng and Anna Ssemuyaba, with Dionne Edwards directing block two.

	“I’m thrilled to come on board and play Ryan in Charmer, working alongside such incredible talent. Tom’s scripts are fantastic, heartfelt, funny and smart. I can’t wait for people to meet the characters that Siena, Connor and Sophie create.”
	

	Added Meghan Lyvers, managing director of scripted originals at Sky: “’Charmer’ is exactly the kind of bold, original storytelling we champion at Sky. Tom has crafted a brilliantly distinctive take on modern love, brought to life by an exceptional cast led by Anthony, Siena, Connor and Sophie. Backed by the combined pedigree of Working Title Television and Story Films, and with Elliot Hegarty at the helm, this outstanding creative team is bringing something provocative and thrilling to the screen. We can’t wait for audiences to see it.”

	“Charmer” is produced by Working Title Television, part of Universal Global Television (a division of Universal Studio Group), and Story Films, part of Banijay Entertainment. Working Title Television’s recent productions include “Too Much” and “Jo Nesbo’s Detective Hole,” while Story Films’ credits include “The Thief, His Wife and The Canoe” and “Deceit.” Executive Producers are Tim Bevan, Eric Fellner, Surian Fletcher-Jones and Simon Hatton for Working Title Television, David Nath and Peter Beard for Story Films, and Thomas Aspell and Elliot Hegarty. Josh Wilkins serves as co-executive producer. Commissioning Editor Manpreet Dosanjh is executive producer for Sky. The series producer is Charlotte Surtees.

	“Charmer” will air on Sky and streaming service Now in the UK and Italy. International sales of the series will be handled by NBCUniversal Global TV Distribution.

	Boyle is repped by B-Side, WME, Tapestry London and Johnson Shapiro Slewett & Kole.

schema.headline: Anthony Boyle to Lead Sky Drama ‘Charmer’ From Working Title, Story Films

title: Patricio Valladares Descends Into Hell With Horror Adaptation of Dante’s ‘Inferno’ (EXCLUSIVE)
description: Chilean filmmaker Patricio Valladares, behind the 2023 found-footage horror pic “Invoking Yell,” is set to direct a fantasy-horror reimagining of Da
body:
Chilean filmmaker Patricio Valladares, behind the 2023 found-footage horror pic “Invoking Yell,” is set to direct a fantasy-horror reimagining of Dante’s “Inferno.”

	“The Divine Comedy,” slated to begin filming in Rome in September, is produced by Italian film company Anxur Films, in collaboration with Ireland’s Skincrawl Studios, which is also handling international sales. 


	“You’ve likely come across the famous line from Dante Alighieri’s masterpiece, ‘Abandon all hope, ye who enter here,’ that Stephen King also borrowed for his novel ‘The Stand,’” reads the logline. The film promises to take audiences through the gates of Hell that bear the infamous inscription.
	



	

	



	Valladares’ adaptation follows Dante, a grieving writer, and Virgil, a former priest, as they descend into the terrifying realm of the dead in search of Dante’s wife Beatrice. 


	As they go through a series of terrifying circles inhabited by the dead and the damned, Dante and Virgil encounter lost souls trapped within eternal punishments shaped by their deepest fears, desires and regrets.

	Pursued by monstrous entities and confronted by manifestations of human suffering, Dante and Virgil will eventually come face to face with the Devil himself.

	Starring Christopher Rygh (“Vikings: Valhalla”), Matthew Metcalfe, Tilda Metsola and Fadhillah Othman, “The Divine Comedy,” Valladares warns, “is set to push the limits of pain and physical torture to levels only seen in Barker’s ‘Hellraiser’ or Xavier Gens’ ‘Frontier(s).’”

	“What drew me to ‘The Divine Comedy’ was the opportunity to create visions of hell that feel physical and painful,” he tells Variety. “But at its core, it’s a very human story about grief, guilt and how far you’re willing to go for love when you have nothing left to lose. The concept itself generates so much atmosphere, tension and real horror.”
	

	Filming begins on Sept. 7 in Rome.

	Ahead of that, Valladares will be celebrating the Aug. 28 world premiere of his new film, “Invoking Scream,” the sequel to “Invoking Yell,” at FrightFest in London.

	Exploring the dark intersections of the supernatural and extreme music, the centers on a trio of metalheads who unwittingly unleash a dark force after they uncover a buried box containing a VHS tape and a mysterious book of witchcraft at the gravesite of Invoking Yell lead singer Andrea Fernandez.  

	“Invoking Scream” stars María Jesús Marcone, Luna Martínez, Teresita Rios and Matías López.

	Valladares is also developing a FMV horror game via his Vallastudio Films that merges analog filmmaking with interactive storytelling.

schema.headline: Patricio Valladares Descends Into Hell With Horror Adaptation of Dante’s ‘Inferno’ (EXCLUSIVE)

title: Pimmada Chaisakcharoen’s Thai Horror ‘Tame’ Launches EST N8, BrandThink’s B-EST Pictures (EXCLUSIVE)
description:
EST N8 and BrandThink have launched B-EST Pictures, a joint venture for feature films and live experiences. 

	The venture’s first title, “Tame,” a
body:
EST N8 and BrandThink have launched B-EST Pictures, a joint venture for feature films and live experiences. 

	The venture’s first title, “Tame,” a horror-suspense feature rooted in Thai folklore, will launch international sales at the Toronto Film Festival‘s market ahead of its Thailand theatrical release on Oct. 29.

	Set in a rural bullfighting village where animals are broken through fear and ritual, “Tame” follows a teenage girl trapped under her family’s control who turns an ancient spirit’s brutal methods back on the people who raised her. The film marks the feature directorial debut of Thamuya Thasananukulkij.
	

	“Tame” is produced by Anucha Boonyawatana, whose credit “Malila: The Farewell Flower” won Busan’s Kim Jiseok Award and the Netpac Award at the Golden Horse Film Festival, alongside BrandThink founder Ekalak “Luck” Klunson, whose credits include Netflix’s “Redlife,” “Halabala” and “5th Round.” The cast is led by T-pop star Pimmada Chaisakcharoen (“Human Resource”), alongside Komchadluek Award winner Chayanit Chansangavej (“Cracked,” “Supposed”) and Jespipat Tilapornputt (“The Stain”).


	B-EST Pictures pairs EST N8’s sales, financing and distribution network with BrandThink’s editorial reach into Thai subcultures and creative communities. The companies will co-develop, co-finance and co-produce films and live experiences, starting in Southeast Asia before expanding into international markets. Three additional titles under the venture will be announced in the coming months.

	“Great stories and cultural movements are happening in Asia every day, but the gap has always been curation and distribution built for an international audience,” said Kris Eiamsakulrat, co-founder of EST N8. “By pairing EST N8’s sales engine with BrandThink’s pulse on youth culture, music and creator communities, we’re positioning B-EST not just to distribute finished content, but to produce the cultural moments that generate it.”
	

	BrandThink was built on the idea of “Creative Change,” said Klunson, the company’s managing director and founder. “In EST N8, we’ve found partners who share our vision for elevating Asian narratives. Launching B-EST Pictures with ‘Tame’ at TIFF lets us turn our editorial instincts into globally distributable IP.”

	Thai horror carries a long track record of international appeal, said Sophie Changhui-Shi, head of studios at EST N8. “‘Tame’ furthers the genre by pairing visceral suspense with deep emotional and cultural resonance. Thamuya’s debut is haunting, provocative and uncompromising.”

	EST N8 operates across film financing, sales and distribution, bringing premium Asian cinema to the global marketplace while also distributing Hollywood and European titles across Asia. Its slate includes Rezwan Shahriar Sumit’s Rotterdam Big Screen Award winner “Master”; Indonesia’s 2026 box office hit “Danur: The Last Chapter”; Kimo Stamboel’s “Janur Ireng”; Tetsuya Mariko’s “Dear Stranger,” starring Hidetoshi Nishijima and Gwei Lun-Mei; Raindance premiere “The Invisible Half”; Chan Chun-hao’s “Dead End”; and “Jaguar,” a Filipino thriller and SXSW Grand Jury Award nominee.

	BrandThink is a Bangkok-based content company spanning publishing, brand partnerships, IP experiences, community and cinema. Its film arm, BrandThink Cinema, produced the 2023 feature “Redlife” and the Netflix original series “Terror Tuesday: Extreme.”

schema.headline: Pimmada Chaisakcharoen’s Thai Horror ‘Tame’ Launches EST N8, BrandThink’s B-EST Pictures (EXCLUSIVE)

title: Oscars: Belgium Selects Lukas Dhont’s Cannes Prizewinning ‘Coward’ for International Feature Race
description: Lukas Dhont’s “Coward,” which won the best actor prize at Cannes for Emmanuel Macchia and Valentin Campagne, will represent Belgium in the internati
body:
Lukas Dhont’s “Coward,” which won the best actor prize at Cannes for Emmanuel Macchia and Valentin Campagne, will represent Belgium in the international feature film race at the 99th Academy Awards.

	The selection marks the third time Belgium has submitted a film by Dhont to the Oscars. His 2018 debut “Girl” – which won Cannes’ Caméra d’Or for best first feature as well as the Queer Palm — was Belgium’s submission, but failed to make the final nomination cut; while “Close” – which won Cannes’ Grand Prize in 2022 — was nominated for best international feature at the Oscars, ultimately losing to “All Quiet on the Western Front.”
	

	Set on the Belgian front during World War I, “Coward” follows Pierre, a young soldier who arrives in 1916 determined to prove himself in battle, and Francis, who stages theatrical performances behind the lines to keep up the troops’ morale. As the violence intensifies, the two men search for ways to escape the brutality surrounding them, if only briefly.


	The movie was lauded at Cannes where it was bought by Mubi for a number of major territories, including the U.S., U.K., Spain, Italy and Latin America.

	“I am truly honored that we get to represent Belgium at the Oscars this year with ‘Coward.’ We look forward to sharing our film with the world and with Belgian audiences,” said Dhont, who has become one of Belgium’s most internationally acclaimed filmmakers.”‘Coward’ celebrates togetherness in broken times, connection in a fragmented world. We hope that ‘Coward,’ which above all celebrates the power of the heart, will offer a moment of tenderness and comfort,” Dhont added.
	

	Dhont once again collaborated on “Coward” with several members of his longtime creative team, including co-writer Angelo Tijssens and cinematographer Frank Van den Eeden, among others. 

	The film was produced by Michiel Dhont for The Reunion, in co-production with Versus in Belgium, Juliette Schrameck at Lumen in France and Topkapi Films in the Netherlands. The Match Factory handles international sales.

	The film will continue its festival run in the coming weeks, notably at Toronto, San Sebastian and BFI London Film Festival. Diaphana will release it in France on Nov. 18, while Mubi is set to release it in North America in December.

schema.headline: Oscars: Belgium Selects Lukas Dhont’s Cannes Prizewinning ‘Coward’ for International Feature Race

title: Crooked Media Is Bringing Back Nate Silver’s ‘FiveThirtyEight Politics’ Podcast, Which Will Relaunch Next Month as ‘Still Counting’ (EXCLUSIVE)
description:
FiveThirtyEight is coming back from the dead — sort of.

	Just ahead of the 2026 midterm elections, Crooked Media inked a deal to acquire and revive
body:
FiveThirtyEight is coming back from the dead — sort of.

	Just ahead of the 2026 midterm elections, Crooked Media inked a deal to acquire and revive the “FiveThirtyEight Politics” podcast hosted by Nate Silver, Clare Malone and Galen Druke. 

	And under Crooked Media’s wing, the show is getting a new name: “Still Counting,” a weekly podcast hosted by the former “FiveThirtyEight Politics” hosts and data journalists. The show premieres Sept. 9 on Spotify, Apple Podcasts, YouTube and other major podcast platforms. “Still Counting” will break down the latest political news and polling, covering not only elections but also topics like betting markets and AI.
	

	Silver founded the FiveThirtyEight blog in 2008, analyzing opinion polls politics and economics, and it became a licensed feature of the New York Times. ESPN acquired the brand in 2013 before it moved over to Disney sister company ABC News in 2018. Silver left ABC News in 2023 amid broader layoffs at Disney. In March 2025, ABC shut down the FiveThirtyEight website and podcasts (and laid off the remaining staff) amid another round of cost-cutting at Disney.


	Now Silver, Malone and Druke are back in the saddle with Crooked Media, the progressive media company best known for “Pod Save America,” hosted by former Obama administration staffers Jon Favreau, Jon Lovett, Tommy Vietor and Dan Pfeiffer. Crooked said the “Still Counting” hosts will bring “a no bullshit, clear-eyed approach to the wonky ins and outs of politics without losing the humor and personality that make the conversation fun.”

	Silver, in the trailer for “Still Counting” (watch below), says: “There’s a ton of data and information coming at us every day, and a surprising amount is misunderstood or under-explained. Numbers are hard, takes are easy. We’re taking a step back to ask: What does the data actually say, and how can we use it to better understand the future of American politics?”
	

	The podcast will explore three key questions, according to Silver: what does the data actually say?; how do we reconcile that with the other things that we’re seeing in American politics and around the world?; and “how do we use that to understand or maybe even dare to predict the future of American politics?”

	“Crooked has always been about finding smart, distinctive voices who can help listeners make sense of a complicated world,” said Lucinda Treat, CEO of Crooked Media. “Nate, Clare and Galen have spent years doing exactly that, bringing rigorous analysis and sharp perspective to the biggest questions in politics and public opinion. We’re thrilled to welcome them to Crooked and bring that work to a new audience of politics and data obsessives.”



	

	



	Silver now writes Silver Bulletin on Substack, covering politics, sports, AI and risk. His most recent book, “On the Edge: The Art of Risking Everything,” is a New York Times bestseller about professional risk-takers like poker players, venture capitalists and the leaders of AI labs.

	Malone is a staff writer at the New Yorker covering media and politics. She previously wrote for FiveThirtyEight, where she reported on class, race and electoral politics, covering the 2016 and 2020 U.S. presidential campaigns.

	Druke is the founder and host of GD POLITICS, a “nonpartisan” podcast and Substack that “explains politics with curiosity, rigor, data and humor.” His reporting and analysis have appeared on outlets including ABC News, the BBC, NPR and MS NOW.

	Watch the trailer for “Still Counting”:

schema.headline: Crooked Media Is Bringing Back Nate Silver’s ‘FiveThirtyEight Politics’ Podcast, Which Will Relaunch Next Month as ‘Still Counting’ (EXCLUSIVE)

title: Oscars: South Korea Selects Lee Chang-dong’s ‘Possible Love’ for International Feature Race
description: The Korean Film Council (KOFIC) has selected “Possible Love,” directed by Lee Chang-dong, as South Korea‘s official entry for the international feat
body:
The Korean Film Council (KOFIC) has selected “Possible Love,” directed by Lee Chang-dong, as South Korea‘s official entry for the international feature film category at the 2027 Academy Awards.

	“Possible Love” marks Lee’s first feature in eight years, following “Burning,” “Poetry” and “Secret Sunshine.” The film centers on two married couples whose lives intersect after a funeral: Mi-ok and her laid-off husband Ho-seok (Sul Kyung-gu), who live quietly with their young son Cheol, and Ye-ji, a filmmaker making a documentary about workers who lost their jobs, and her husband Sang-woo (Zo In-sung). When Mi-ok agrees to be filmed by Ye-ji, the two women grow close, while Mi-ok finds herself unsettled by an attraction to Sang-woo. As the two couples’ worlds overlap, cracks begin to surface in both marriages.
	

	A 15-member selection committee, chaired by film critic Jung Sung-il, made the choice. Other committee members included Kang Myung-chan, Kim So-young, Kim Jae-joong, Kim Tae-sung, Kim Hyun-chul, Moon Young-hwa, Song Kyung-won, Won Dong-yeon, Yoo Hyun-taek, Yoon Sung-eun, Lee Han, Lim Dae-hyung, Jung Yi-jun and Cho Hwa-sung.


	In its evaluation, the committee cited the film’s polished craftsmanship and the clarity of its directorial vision, pointing to the tone and mise-en-scène that sustain a sense of pressure throughout the story. The drama was described as prompting reflection on gentle forms of violence, incomplete freedom and the nature of true happiness, alongside a labor movement sequence that the committee said captured layered social undercurrents.
	

	The committee also highlighted the film’s humanism and delicate direction, its dense, multidimensional character relationships, and its meditation on love, desire and original sin. Members called it the culmination of Lee’s perspective and preoccupations as a filmmaker, praising what they described as nearly flawless performances from the four leads.

	The committee pointed to the international feature category’s track record of favoring auteur-driven dramas, noting that Lee’s 2018 film “Burning” became the first Korean title to advance to the Academy’s foreign language film shortlist. Members also flagged strong anticipation from North American press and said a Netflix awards team is preparing a campaign for the film that extends to a best picture push.

	The film’s world premiere will be at the Venice Film Festival and North American Premiere at the Toronto Film Festival.

	Under Academy international feature film category rules, “Possible Love” must complete its local theatrical release in South Korea by Sept. 30. The film will open in Korean theaters Sept. 23, followed by select theatrical releases in Australia Oct. 22 and in the U.S., Canada, U.K., Ireland and Japan Oct. 23, before streaming globally on Netflix starting Nov. 6.

	South Korea has submitted films in the category since 1962 without a nomination for decades, until Lee Chang-dong’s “Burning” became the first Korean film to make the shortlist in 2018. Bong Joon Ho’s “Parasite” then won the category and best picture in 2020 – the first non-English-language film to do so – and Park Chan-wook’s “Decision to Leave” (2022) and “No Other Choice” (2025) both reached the shortlist without landing a nomination. 

	The 99th Academy Awards are scheduled for March 14, 2027.

schema.headline: Oscars: South Korea Selects Lee Chang-dong’s ‘Possible Love’ for International Feature Race

title: ‘NAZA’ Documentary From ‘No Other Land’ Directors Acquired by MK2 Films Ahead of Venice Film Festival Premiere
description: French sales company MK2 Films has boarded “NAZA,” the new hot-button documentary from “No Other Land” directors Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor that
body:
French sales company MK2 Films has boarded “NAZA,” the new hot-button documentary from “No Other Land” directors Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor that was added on Monday to the Venice Film Festival competition lineup.

	The doc, which was shot at night on the rooftops of Tel Aviv, shows “in detail the systems behind Israel’s calculated mass killing of Palestinian civilians in Gaza,” according to its official synopsis.


	“NAZA,” the film’s title, is a term that appears throughout the documentary. “It is a military acronym euphemistically used by Israeli intelligence to indicate the number of civilians that it expects will be killed in an airstrike,” according to a MK2 Films statement.
	

	The film — which is the only documentary feature in this year’s Venice’s competition lineup — is produced by British newspaper The Guardian and James Wilson (JW Films) and executive produced by Jonathan Glazer. Wilson and Glazer are the Oscar-winning team behind the film “The Zone of Interest.”

	Abraham and Szor are the two Israeli co-directors of “No Other Land,” which won the 2025 best documentary Oscar. The other two “No Other Land” co-directors, Hamdan Ballal and Basel Adra, are Palestinian. “No Other Land,” which premiered at the Berlin Film Festival, showed the gradual demolition of Palestinian houses and villages in the Masafer Yatta region of the West Bank by Israeli military bulldozers. 

	“NAZA” builds on revelations first published by the Israeli-Palestinian publication +972, Hebrew-language outlet Local Call and The Guardian between 2023 and 2025, according to promotional materials. The potentially explosive doc will premiere in Venice on Sept. 10.
	

	Nathanaël Karmitz, CEO of MK2, and Fionnuala Jamison, managing director, said: “Beyond the power of its testimonies and the rigor of its journalistic approach, the film by Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor struck us for the cinematic excellence of its form. The intelligence of its direction resonates deeply with MK2’s history as a film company whose mission has always included giving audiences, through cinema, the keys and tools to confront the truth of the world we live in, however difficult that truth may be.”

	“NAZA” is a Guardian production with JW Films, in association with Placeholder Films and Unseen Hand.

	The 83rd Venice Film Festival runs from Sept. 2 to 12.

schema.headline: ‘NAZA’ Documentary From ‘No Other Land’ Directors Acquired by MK2 Films Ahead of Venice Film Festival Premiere

            Brian Hickerson's magnetic charm kept Hayden Panettiere coming back to him despite their rocky relationship over the years, according to Brian's half-sister.
      
    
            Ashley Hickerson told the Daily Mail ... “If I can say one thing about Brian, it’s that he is the most charismatic person and he draws you in.” Ashley also said she understood why Hayden was with Brian, who's fun and can make you laugh no matter what.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Hayden and Brian began dating in 2018 and stayed together on and off until the actresss' suspected overdose death on August 16 in Greenville, South Carolina. Brian and his brother, Zach, found Hayden's body and called 911. Her cause and manner of death are pending the results of toxicology tests.
      
    
            As you know, Brian had a history of domestic violence against Hayden, who accused him of punching her in 2020, according to court docs, obtained by TMZ.
      

            The docs say Hayden called the cops on Brian after an argument turned physical in their L.A. apartment. Bryan was arrested and charged with felony domestic violence, but he later reached a global resolution in that case and one in Wyoming. He was sentenced to 360 days in jail with 358 days suspended, and he also served 12 months of unsupervised probation.
      
    
            Court docs reveal that Bryan even sent Hayden threatening text messages after his 2020 arrest for domestic violence. In addition, Brian was reportedly arrested in 2010 and charged with assault and battery by mob, which did not involve violence against Hayden.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Brian's sister, Ashley, told the Daily Mail ... “He did seek treatment and he was getting help. He did own up to his s–t.” Ashley went on ... 'We all have our demons. Brian was not raised that way. It wasn't until he got into drugs that he went south."

            His death is described as a "sudden and heartbreaking loss" in a GoFundMe launched for his family to help cover funeral and burial expenses.
